interface.signature: findOrder(dict: List[str], N: int, K: int) -> str

preconditions.description: The number of words in the dictionary is between 1 and 300.
The number of starting alphabets is between 1 and 26.
The length of each word in the dictionary is between 1 and 50.
All words in the dictionary are in lowercase.

preconditions.expression: isinstance(dict, list) and all(isinstance(word, str) for word in dict)
preconditions.description: The input dictionary is a list of strings.
The number of words N is an integer between 1 and 300.
The number of starting alphabets K is an integer between 1 and 26.

postconditions.description: The length of the returned string is equal to the number of starting alphabets K.

postconditions.expression: all(char in return_value for char in string.ascii_lowercase[:K])
postconditions.description: The returned string contains all the starting alphabets and only those alphabets.
Each character in the returned string appears only once.

postconditions.expression: all(dict[i] < dict[i+1] for i in range(N-1) if dict[i] != dict[i+1])
postconditions.description: The order of characters in the returned string is consistent with the order of the words in the dictionary.
The output is 1 if the order of characters returned by the function is correct, otherwise 0.
